chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about wine, in which something is done until it acidifies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If that which was done in it is dominant over what was made in it, then there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (specifically grape wine, often implying impurity until transformation)
key_terms.تُحَمِّض: To become acidic / to turn into vinegar
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for wine to be considered validly transformed into vinegar according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the criterion for the transformation of wine (khamr) into vinegar (khal), ruling that the addition must be dominant to effect a valid change, a principle central to Shia fiqh regarding impurity (najasa) and purity (taha). This hadith highlights the juristic distinction between mere alteration and complete transformation, ensuring that the resulting vinegar is not only permissible for consumption but also pure for use in prayer. It reflects the Shia emphasis on objective physical changes rather than subjective intent when determining legal status.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the wine, something is done in it until it acidifies. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If that which was done in it, it overcame upon what was made in it, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Bukayr from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about wine to which something is done until it is turned sour. He (the Imam) said, ’If what is done in it (the wine) overwhelms it, then is not harmful/”
